newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani Kashmir orders gang-rape probe.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani Kashmir orders gang-rape probe.

text.p: Authorities in Pakistan-ruled Kashmir said on Saturday they were probing an alleged gang-rape by members of one tribe against another.
Members of the Qureshi tribe said rival Sudhans sexually assaulted them because they objected to a love affair between a Qureshi man and a Sudhan woman.
They told Reuters that eight women and four men from the Qureshi tribe, whom Sudhans regard as racially inferior, were sexually assaulted at Soon Topa in Azad (free) Kashmir between June 16 and 18.
At least 70 people, including 30 women and 25 children, were also banished from their native village by a Sudhan tribal council as a punishment for the love affair, the alleged victims said.

"We were raped by several people for over two days before we were forced to leave our homes," Zubaida, a 24-year-old mother of three, told Reuters at Chakra village, some 40 km (25 miles) west of Islamabad, where she said her family had fled after being banished.
"They locked me in a separate room and several people raped me before I fell unconscious," she said, weeping.
"My children were crying with hunger when I gained my senses. When I asked for food, they just gave a few morsels of bread left by their dogs and cats," she said.
Azad Kashmir Prime Minister Sultan Mahmud told reporters in Islamabad he had been informed by police that there was no case of gang rape and that the incident had been exaggerated.
But he said he had sent the leader of a political party that is a partner in his coalition government to investigate the matter and report to him.
"I assure you, and I assure the families, that no injustice will be done," he said.
